ov: About 50 species of squirrels that glide between trees on a furred membrane stretching from wrist to ankle, steering with their limbs and tail. Most are nocturnal. They cannot truly fly, but can cover a forest faster than tree squirrels.
rg: North America and Asia; the Siberian flying squirrel reaches northeast Europe (Russia, Finland and Estonia).
df: Fruit, seeds, buds, flowers, insects, snails and spiders.

cf.tip: The sugar glider looks and glides much like a flying squirrel, but it is a marsupial, not a squirrel.

fx: In 2019 a flying squirrel was found by chance to glow pink under UV light; ordinary squirrels do not.
A cartilage spur on each wrist, found only in flying squirrels, helps hold the gliding membrane out.
